content: Regular foot evaluations are crucial to identify potential risk factors for the development of foot ulcers and the need for amputations. Comprehensive foot examinations should include assessments of the skin, sensory function, peripheral pulses, and neurological status. Patients who have experienced sensory loss or have active foot ulcers should undergo foot evaluations during every clinical visit. Individuals with a history of foot-related complications should be provided with appropriate and protective footwear to prevent further issues. Vascular screening is advised for patients presenting with foot-related symptoms or those who have risk factors for peripheral arterial disease (PAD). For patients at high risk of foot complications, specialized foot care should be offered, which may include custom-designed footwear and advanced therapeutic interventions.
